reviews.comment: Super hard grader. Instruction on syllables was never clarified.
RUN THE OTHER WAY
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Treats students like children, creative workshops have to be done HER way, interrupts students constantly, students do the lecturing not her, she will organize class one way and then get mad at us for doing what she asked because there's not enough time, talks over class time constantly and gets upset when you leave, late to class often

Never take this professor if you like organization. She is impossible to get in touch with outside of class. Don't even bother emailing. Feedback on assignments is either non-existent or extremely unhelpful. The rubrics for assignments are either never created or cause more confusion than if you didn't have it in the first place.

The best class of my semester; I can't recommend this prof and class enough! Please take this class if you need a literature credit! She is the best, such a relaxing learning environment, she's very laid back! There are no tests, just two essays and a few discussions and she has a great grading scale. We had to read a few books, she explains them.

Professor Bhattacharya was nice! This class was the easiest thing ever. I didn't touch any of the books we read (oops) and I made an A. She is super understanding and extends time for assignments. There is no homework except for a discussion question after each class, but she grades them easily. The tests are just short essays which aren't bad.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Constantly changes her requirements. If you call her out on it, she's hostile. If you ask for clarification, she's hostile. She has a horrible attitude for a professor. She acted appalled that we had the audacity to want a review for the exam. Her communication is nonexistent. The class is easy but not worth it to get talked down to all semester.

ENGL/AFST 379 is cross-listed as an Africana Studies course, however, there is no Africana Studies in this course. There are a lot of readings, a lot of discussion posts, and a lot of confusion. There was a lot of miscommunication problems adding more difficulty than needed to be. If you aren't able to read a novel once a week, try another course.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Bhattacharya makes her lectures interesting, and is good about answering questions. She can sometimes though be vague in her instructions. This class was fairly easy (I didn't complete a majority of the books and got an A). The class was interesting and this professor is great - I would definitely recommend taking it if you need an ENGL class
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Possibly the worst communication I've received from a prof ever. She gives vague instructions and then sends passive aggressive emails when we don't do exactly what she wants. The discussions are micromanaged by her, which makes it very quiet. It's an easy A, but honestly not worth the anxiety that comes with each miscommunication.

I really enjoyed ENGL 374 with this professor. The novels she picked were very interesting, and the class requirements were standard for an english class at this level. The transition to online class (due to Covid-19) was a little rough for all of us, but I would take the class again anytime.

This class is an easy A, but the professor is very disorganized (some due to COVID-19). She would forget to post discussion boards or quizzes or take a long time to grade exams. It can be frustrating to deal with but in my opinion this class is worth it. The quizzes and debates are easy and there is only one exam at the end of the semester.

I think this was Nandini's first time teaching a large English class, and it didn't really work? We had group debates, and that doesn't really work in a large class. It was kind of a hot mess. Unclear instructions and mass confusion in the GroupMe. She's a nice lady, though, so maybe try her in a smaller class? Books were all about dystopias.

Dr. B is a nice lady. She didn't seem very prepared for class every day, just sort of talking or making us lead the lectures. The books she chose for this semester was rough though. None were very engaging or interesting, make it hard to spark interest in the class. But you only have a couple quizzes and debates and no exams so the grades are good

WOW, best professor I have ever had!!!!! She is the coolest ever. So easy to understand, her lectures are easy she is fun to talk with. Extra credit and responds fast when grading and emails. My friend and I sat in the back and still were able to get really good grades. I emailed her when problems arise and she was quick to respond and fix them.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Really nice professor and person. She really does care about the students. Would defiantly take again given the opportunity.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class overall is not bad at all. She tries to diversify the lectures so it is not always her talking at you. Make sure you read the stories and understand it for the test and for the pop quizzes.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I really loved the class I took with Dr. Bhattacharya. Not an exceptionally difficult grader, but not an easy A by any means. She is one of the most brilliant people I've met - there were so many times she turned a student's babbling claims into clear, coherent ideas that advanced me understanding of the subject at hand. A lovely person and prof.
Most classes were discussions of the book, while the rest were students presenting their book reviews. She also had several days that were online discussions.
Class was mostly just discussions about the readings. Tons of extra credit to be earned. Super easy A.
